title: Eukaryote supergroups and their mitochondrial genomes (consensus after Burki et al. 2020)
summary: Cladogram of eukaryotic supergroups (topology after Burki et al. 2020, with Provora added after Tikhonenkov et al. 2022). The root of the eukaryote tree is unresolved; the tree is drawn with Discoba branching first only for convenience. Each tip carries a summary of what mitochondrial genomes look like in that lineage: size range, number of protein-coding genes, genetic code and notable peculiarities. Hover a tip for details.

Jakobida.name: Jakobida
Jakobida.note: The most bacteria-like mtDNAs known: 60–100 kb, 62–66 protein genes (Andalucia godoyi 67.6 kb, 100 genes incl. 66 proteins; Reclinomonas americana 69 kb, 97 genes) incl. a bacterial-type multisubunit RNA polymerase (rpoA–D), tufA, secY, tatC and many ribosomal proteins; Shine–Dalgarno-like motifs; standard genetic code (Lang 1997; Burger 2013).

Heterolobosea.name: Heterolobosea
Heterolobosea.note: Naegleria gruberi: ~50 kb, ~46 protein genes; Acrasis: extensive gene loss/transfer. Standard code.

Euglenozoa.name: Euglenozoa
Euglenozoa.note: Bizarre architectures: kinetoplastids have a maxicircle (~20–40 kb, ~18 proteins, many cryptogenes) + thousands of minicircles encoding guide RNAs for U-insertion/deletion editing; diplonemids split genes into modules on separate chromosomes joined by trans-splicing; Euglena has fragmented genes. Standard code.

Metamonada.name: Metamonada
Metamonada.note: No mitochondrial genome at all: mitosomes/hydrogenosomes (Giardia, Trichomonas) lack DNA; Monocercomonoides has lost the organelle entirely (Karnkowska 2016).

Malawimonadida.name: Malawimonadida
Malawimonadida.note: Malawimonas jakobiformis: ~47 kb, ~50 protein genes, gene-rich but lacks the jakobid bacterial RNA polymerase. Standard code.

Amoebozoa.name: Amoebozoa
Amoebozoa.note: Dictyostelium discoideum 55.6 kb (~40 proteins), Acanthamoeba castellanii 41.6 kb (~33 proteins, code 4); Physarum uses C-insertion RNA editing.

Apusomonadida.name: Apusomonadida
Apusomonadida.note: Thecamonas trahens: gene-rich mtDNA with many ribosomal-protein genes; standard code.

Breviatea.name: Breviatea
Breviatea.note: Anaerobic; Pygsuia has hydrogenosome-like organelles; mtDNA highly reduced/absent in some.

Fungi.name: Fungi
Fungi.note: 19–235 kb (mostly introns and ORFs), typically 14 core proteins (cox1–3, cob, atp6/8/9, nad1–6/4L) plus rps3; loss of complex I in Saccharomycetales/Schizosaccharomyces; mould code (table 4, UGA=Trp) in most; Allomyces/Rhizophydium (chytrids) more gene-rich.

Ichthyosporea.name: Ichthyosporea (+Filasterea)
Ichthyosporea.note: Amoebidium parasiticum: hundreds of linear chromosomes, >200 kb total; Capsaspora ~ 197 kb; Sphaeroforma.

Choanoflagellata.name: Choanoflagellata
Choanoflagellata.note: Monosiga brevicollis 76.6 kb, 55 genes including several ribosomal proteins; standard code.

Metazoa.name: Metazoa
Metazoa.note: Bilaterians: compact 14–20 kb circles, 13 proteins (cox1–3, cob, atp6/8, nad1–6/4L), 2 rRNAs, 22 tRNAs; genetic codes 2/4/5/9/13/14/… (Boore 1999). Non-bilaterians differ: cnidarians (linear, code 4, few tRNAs), sponges (up to 25 kb, extra genes), Trichoplax 43 kb with introns (Lavrov & Pett 2016).

CRuMs.name: CRuMs
CRuMs.note: Collodictyonids, rigifilids, Mantamonas: gene-rich mtDNAs (e.g. Diphylleia rotans), retaining many ribosomal-protein genes.

Glaucophyta.name: Glaucophyta
Glaucophyta.note: Cyanophora paradoxa 51.6 kb, ~ 33 protein genes; Glaucocystis larger.

Rhodophyta.name: Rhodophyta
Rhodophyta.note: 25–35 kb, 24–27 protein genes, highly conserved gene order (Chondrus crispus 25.8 kb; Porphyra purpurea 36.8 kb); Cyanidiales similar.

Chlorophyta.name: Chlorophyta
Chlorophyta.note: Extreme variation: prasinophytes ~45 kb, gene-rich (Nephroselmis olivacea 45.2 kb) vs Chlamydomonas reinhardtii 15.8 kb linear, 7 proteins, fragmented rRNAs; some Sphaeropleales/Ulvophyceae with expanded genomes; non-standard codes in some (Zíhala & Eliáš 2019).

Streptophyta.name: Streptophyta (land plants + charophytes)
Streptophyta.note: Land plants: 200 kb to >11 Mb (Silene conica 11.3 Mb; Sloan 2012), yet only ~40 protein genes; huge intergenic regions, foreign DNA, recombination, C→U RNA editing, multichromosomal structures. Charophytes 40–70 kb, gene-rich (Chara vulgaris 67.7 kb). Standard code.

Cryptista.name: Cryptista
Cryptista.note: Rhodomonas salina 48 kb (~45 proteins), Hemiselmis andersenii 60 kb; gene-rich, bacterial-like gene clusters.

Haptista.name: Haptista
Haptista.note: Emiliania huxleyi 29 kb, ~20 protein genes; Chrysochromulina similar; centrohelid mtDNAs are larger and more gene-rich.

Telonemia.name: Telonemia
Telonemia.note: Sister lineage of SAR (together TSAR); gene-rich mitogenome, only recently characterised.

Stramenopiles.name: Stramenopiles
Stramenopiles.note: 35–58 kb, ~35–40 protein genes incl. many ribosomal proteins (Phytophthora infestans 37.9 kb; diatoms 35–45 kb; brown algae 35–58 kb; Cafeteria 43 kb; Thraustochytrium ~ 40 kb). Standard code.

Alveolata.name: Alveolata
Alveolata.note: Ciliates: linear ~47 kb, ~44 proteins, split genes (Tetrahymena), code 4. Apicomplexa: the smallest mtDNAs, ~6 kb linear tandem repeats with only cox1, cox3, cob and fragmented rRNAs (Plasmodium; Feagin 2012). Dinoflagellates: same three genes, massively fragmented and edited (Waller & Jackson 2009). Chromera/Vitrella: 2 genes.

Rhizaria.name: Rhizaria
Rhizaria.note: Bigelowiella natans (chlorarachniophyte) ~40 kb; foraminiferan and radiolarian mtDNAs remain poorly known.

Provora.name: Provora
Provora.note: Newly recognised supergroup of predatory flagellates (Tikhonenkov 2022); Ancoracysta twista mtDNA 55 kb with 47 protein genes — among the most gene-rich outside jakobids (Janouškovec 2017).

Hemimastigophora.name: Hemimastigophora
Hemimastigophora.note: Hemimastix kukwesjijk and Spironema: mitochondrial genome data indicate a gene-rich mtDNA; complete genomes still poorly characterised.

root.title: Eukaryotes (LECA)
root.note: Position of the root is uncertain (Burki 2020); LECA already had a mitochondrion with a genome broadly resembling that of jakobids in gene content.

Diaphoretickes.title: Diaphoretickes
Diaphoretickes.note: positions of Provora and Hemimastigophora within Diaphoretickes are uncertain (shown as a polytomy)
